cards.explanation: The answer is an upper room where they're staying. Acts 1:13 says they went to the upper room where they were staying. They came back to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives (Acts 1:12) and headed to a room with a little altitude. I respect any room that comes with altitude, friends.

The answer is eleven. Count them off, friends: Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James. That Judas is a different man from the one Peter talks about later. One chair in the circle is empty, and that's what this whole passage is about.

The word is prayer. Acts 1:14 says, “With one accord they all continued in prayer…” Notice the words “With one accord…” They're all stirring the same bowl in the same direction, bakers. And they keep at it. They continue.

The answer is Mary the mother of Jesus and His brothers. Acts 1:14 says they prayed “…along with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.” So the room is bigger than just the eleven, friends. It's a full house, and everybody in it is praying.

The answer is about a hundred and twenty. Acts 1:15 says it was “a gathering of about a hundred and twenty…” That's a lot of people standing around while Peter stands up. And notice it says “about,” so I won't claim it's an exact headcount, friends.

The word is arrested. Peter says Judas “…became a guide for those who arrested Jesus.” (Acts 1:16) Peter is stating what Judas did, and he says it plainly. It's a sad line, friends, and I think Peter knows it.

The answer is False. Peter says, “He was one of our number and shared in this ministry.” (Acts 1:17) Judas wasn't an outsider, friends. He was counted with them and shared in the work. I think that's why this part is so sad.

The word is Blood. Acts 1:19 says the people in Jerusalem called the field Akeldama in their own language, that is, Field of Blood. I think this part of the story is heavy, friends. We'll let it be heavy and move on gently.

The answer is True! Peter quotes two lines from the book of Psalms, and the second one is “May another take his position.” (Acts 1:20) So there's an empty position that someone else can fill, bakers. That's where the story turns next.

The answer is from John the Baptist's baptism until Jesus was taken up. Peter says the man must have been with them “…beginning from John’s baptism until the day Jesus was taken up from us.” (Acts 1:22) That's a long stretch of time, friends, and he's got to have been there for all of it. Missing a few weeks of the show wouldn't count.
The answer is True. Peter says, “For one of these must become a witness with us of His resurrection.” (Acts 1:22) A witness tells what he saw, friends. And what he has to tell is that Jesus rose.

The answer is that they pray to the Lord. Acts 1:24 says, “And they prayed…” and then they ask the Lord to show them which of the two He has chosen. Two names are on the table, and they take it to the Lord, friends. I do the same before I open the oven.

The word is heart. They pray, “Lord, You know everyone’s heart. Show us which of these two You have chosen” (Acts 1:24) They ask the One who knows hearts to show them, bakers. That's the whole request.
The answer is False. The text doesn't mention a vote. It says, “Then they cast lots, and the lot fell to Matthias.” (Acts 1:26) Nobody's raising a hand or counting ballots in this passage, friends.

The answer is Matthias. “Then they cast lots, and the lot fell to Matthias. So he was added to the eleven apostles.” (Acts 1:26) That's the whole decision, friends, in one verse. And now the twelfth chair is filled.
